root_cause.text: netfs_read_unlock_folios() in the netfs buffered-read collector used EOF (rreq->i_size) instead of the folio boundary to decide a folio was fully collected, causing a folio containing EOF to be unlocked before the later ZERO subrequest had cleared the remainder of the folio.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `fend = umin(fpos + fsize, rreq->i_size);` to `fend = fpos + fsize;`, and the commit/CVE explicitly states that `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` unlocked a folio when collected results reached EOF even though the ZERO subreq beyond EOF "happens after," allowing mmap to observe the uncleared tail.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the full folio end offset in `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` instead of clamping it to `i_size` so folio processing covers the complete folio range.
intent_record.what: The assignment of `fend` in `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` was changed from `umin(fpos + fsize, rreq->i_size)` to `fpos + fsize`, removing the clamp to `rreq->i_size`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the computed end position for the folio now always spans the full folio range instead of being truncated at the file size, allowing subsequent logic and tracing in this path to treat the folio as covering its entire allocated extent even when it extends past EOF.

grouping_result.intent: Use the full folio end offset in `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` instead of clamping it to `i_size` so folio processing covers the complete folio range.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it stops using EOF/i_size to determine folio completion in netfs_read_unlock_folios() and instead uses the full folio boundary, preventing premature unlock of a folio that contains EOF before ZERO processing finishes.

candidates.rationale: This line truncates the folio end to EOF (rreq->i_size) instead of using the full folio boundary, which makes a folio containing EOF appear fully collected too early and allows it to be unlocked before the ZERO subrequest clears the remainder.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement incorrectly clamps the folio end offset to EOF (`rreq->i_size`) inside `netfs_read_unlock_folios()`. As a result, a folio that spans past EOF is treated as fully collected once processing reaches EOF, even though the portion from EOF to the end of the folio has not yet been zeroed by the later ZERO subrequest. That premature completion decision leads to the folio being unlocked too early.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `netfs_read_unlock_folios()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present in the folio-completion test: `fend = umin(fpos + fsize, rreq->i_size);` followed by `if (collected_to < fend) break;` and the comment `/* Unlock any folio we've transferred all of. */`. This uses `rreq->i_size` (EOF) to cap `fend`, meaning for a folio containing EOF, the function treats the folio as complete once data has been collected only up to EOF rather than up to the folio boundary `fpos + fsize`. It then immediately calls `netfs_unlock_read_folio(rreq, folioq, slot);`, unlocking the folio before any later ZERO/clear-tail handling would necessarily have cleared the remainder of that folio. That matches the root cause exactly: deciding a folio was fully collected based on EOF instead of the folio boundary. There is no fix here to defer unlock until the full folio boundary is handled; instead the EOF-capped boundary is the active criterion. Therefore `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the folio-unlock decision logic in `netfs_consume_read_data()` and the EOF/tail-zeroing handling in `netfs_read_subreq_terminated()`. The vulnerable construct is present: folios are unlocked based on whether the collected range reaches the folio boundary, without waiting for any later ZERO subrequest that clears data beyond EOF. Specifically, in `netfs_consume_read_data()`, the code computes `fend = fpos + fsize` and unlocks when `if (start + avail >= fend) { if (fpos == start) { ... netfs_unlock_read_folio(...); ... } }`. Here `avail` is derived from `subreq->transferred` (plus donations), not from completion of a separate zeroing operation. The EOF handling is separate in `netfs_read_subreq_terminated()`: `if (error == 0 && subreq->transferred < subreq->len && (test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_HIT_EOF, &subreq->flags) || test_bit(NETFS_SREQ_CLEAR_TAIL, &subreq->flags))) { netfs_clear_unread(subreq); subreq->transferred = subreq->len; }`. And `netfs_clear_unread()` sets EOF based on `if (subreq->start + subreq->transferred >= subreq->rreq->i_size) __set_bit(NETFS_SREQ_HIT_EOF, &subreq->flags);`, i.e. EOF (`rreq->i_size`) is part of the logic rather than using the folio boundary as the criterion for when it is safe to unlock the folio. There is no visible check preventing unlock of a folio containing EOF until a later ZERO subrequest has cleared the remainder of that folio. Therefore the buggy behavior is present and the fix is not yet in this code.
